result.decisiveNextEvidence: The smallest falsifier for H-NOTOOL: reproduce the no-Tool structured-result Run with read-only observation instrumented at the ToolBridge boundary, perturb the single control/state field under test (one orthogonal axis at a time per run), and observe whether the misclassified correction event toggles. A discriminating result is already obtained if two runs — differing only in which Harness-owned state field was preset — produce opposite termination outcomes; this is a 2–3 run, cheap, owner-native, reversible experiment that closes the causal question.
result.reason: H-NOTOOL is the smallest falsifiable causal target: a real no-Tool Run already misclassified at a ToolBridge boundary, and the owner has a bounded reproduction request with read-only discovery first. This is a reproduced burden (prior 1) — not a hypothetical — and the falsifier is tiny: identify the exact Harness-owned control/state interaction causal to the illegal boundary termination. Closed-loop evidence cost is low (owner-native reproduction exists), reversible (read-only, no authority weakening), and frontier-changing: it discriminates whether Harness control handling or World semantics caused the correction, which no other card tests. H-DISCOVERY ranks second — it is real and quantified but not yet narrowed to a discriminating observation; it needs more candidate-generation before a cheap falsifier exists. R-WITNESS third: real exploit-context but stated as open-ended 'can X evade' rather than a terminal falsifier. S-UNKNOWN fourth: a narrow adapter patch, modest frontier value. HOST-PKG fifth: semantic-compat evidence is already observed; marginal package count is not frontier-changing. Deferred: F-LIVE (consequence-bearing real-capital work with ambiguous-outcome reconciliation — high cost, low information per unit, and owner authority is not yet clear) and G-HUMAN (0/11 responses; evidence is gated on external human availability, not on our budget).
